newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks close higher, but trail New York.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks close higher, but trail New York.

text.p: Toronto's key stock index climbed more than 50 points on Tuesday aided by rebounding gold issues, but lagged the rally on Wall Street.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 Composite Index jumped 51.72 points to 6580.84, trailing the Dow Jones Industrial Average, which soared almost 104 points to 7962.
"It's following the strength in New York...(and) getting a little bit of relief from the gold sector," said Peter Chandler, senior vice-president of brokerage C.M. Oliver & Co. Ltd.
Declining issues edged advancers 499 to 496, while 296 closed flat.

Toronto's resource-laden market got some respite from weaker gold bullion prices, which bounced back from 12-year lows on Monday. The closely watched Comex price in New York added $2 to $321 on Tuesday.
"We're getting a bounce there," Chandler said. But a trader added that bullion prices, and therefore gold stocks, would likely return to a downward trend soon.
Volume totaled 98 million shares worth C$1.8 billion ($1.3 billion).

Only three of Toronto's 14 sub-sectors shed points: pipelines, consumer products and real estate. The rest traveled higher including golds, which climbed 2.2 percent, transportation, forestry products and influential banks.
Canada's two largest gold miners rose on the back of firmer bullion prices. Placer Dome Inc. added 0.85 to 20.10 and Barrick Gold Corp., the world's third biggest gold producer, rose 1.65 to 29.45.
Bank of Montreal rose 1.05 to 57.40 in active dealings after announcing a C$2.5 billion ($1.8 billion) shelf offering program to issue debt securities in Canada and the United States.

IPL Energy Inc. was halted for the session. The Calgary, Alberta-based firm said it acquired a 32 percent stake in Quebec holding company Noverco Inc., making a major push into the province's natural gas business.

Fletcher Challenge Canada Ltd., a subsidiary of the New Zealand forestry firm Fletcher Challenge Ltd., rose 0.80 to 22.80 in light trading as it braced for a strike by unionized workers at its three British Columbia pulp and paper mills.
